 With polls showing a deadlocked race between Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms and Republican Rick Jackson, split-ticket voters could be pivotal. Listen to this article 00:00 00:00 Former President Barack Obama held a rally with Sen. Jon Ossoff and gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms in Morrow, Georgia, less than a week before Election Day.  Elijah Nouvelage / Bloomberg via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 30, 2026, 1:00 PM EDT By Adam Edelman ATLANTA — In Georgia’s race for governor, split-ticket voters could play a decisive role.
